'''Michel Duflo''' (born 1943) is a French mathematician who works in the representation theory of [[Lie group]]s.

== Life ==
From 1962, Duflo studied at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] and received a doctorate under the supervision of [[Jacques Dixmier]]. Currently, he is an [[emeritus professor]] at the [[University of Paris VII]] (Denis Diderot) at the [[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche|Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu]], and at the École normale supérieure.

Duflo has worked on the [[orbit method]] of [[Alexandre Kirillov|Alexander Kirillov]]. He introduced the [[Duflo isomorphism]], an isomorphism between the center of the enveloping algebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra and the invariants of its symmetric algebra.

In 1974 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Vancouver]] (''Inversion formula and invariant differential operators on solvable Lie groups''). Duflo received the [[Prix Le Conte]] of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]; in 1986 he became a corresponding member of the Academy.

His students include [[Laurent Clozel]].

His daughter is the [[Nobel Prize in Economics|Nobel prize]]-winning economist [[Esther Duflo]].
